title: Why Stars Collapse and What Black Holes Are

cues.text: A star is a constant battle between two forces.
Inside, nuclear fusion, the burning of fuel, creates a massive outward push that keeps the star inflated.
At the same time, gravity, the natural attraction of mass, is constantly pulling everything toward the center.
When the star runs out of fuel, the outward push disappears.
Gravity wins, and the entire star collapses inward at incredible speed.
A massive star is truly enormous, sometimes over a hundred times the mass of our sun.
But the singularity at the center of a black hole is crushed into a point of effectively zero volume,
The black hole itself isn't the singularity.
It's the event horizon, a boundary around that point from which nothing, not even light, can escape.
Gravity isn't just a mysterious pull. It is mass warping the fabric of space itself.
Think of a heavy ball on a rubber sheet. It creates a dip, and things nearby naturally slide toward it.
It is not empty space doing the pulling, but the curvature created by the mass that draws everything in.
